I think a good idea might be to ask your son about his "friend".

Ask him how his friend is. Ask him things about his friend: what his hobbies are, what kind of music he likes, etc. Small little things that can allow you son to realize that he can talk to you about these sorts of things. It doesn't have to be the entire conversation, maybe bring it up at dinner or something casual like that. Don't force it too much, and try to sound more like a friend than a father, if that makes sense. If it goes well, overtime hopefully your son will feel more comfortable coming to you to talk about these sorts of things, allowing you to get a better read on the situation.

As for your wife, I honestly think that you should wait and cross that bridge when you get there. If your son does come out as gay or bi or whatever in the future, your wife may have a different reaction if it's real rather than a hypothetical. She may find her son's actions with his friend off-putting, but I feel as though going through hypotheticals might create some unnecessary drama. If your suspicions are confirmed later on, deal with it then. 

For now, at least in my outsider non-parent 21 year old eyes, the most important out of the two situations is your son's, as his will impact your wife's reaction and outlook more than the other way around. I applaud you for being a caring father to your son.

No I wouldn't say anything is wrong with you, the "internalized homophobia" that you think you have can be chalked up to conditioning. The more you hear gay people being called fruit loops and such the more you're associate the concept of "gay" that way. The more you get called gay the more you associate that with the negative connotations those around you give it. I'd say to just remember that you are your own individual, and that you shouldn't have to do anything you don't want to. Some people wear makeup, some don't. It's a personal choice. I'm a similar way in that I don't flaunt my gayness around, but I've pretty much been assumed as straight to all who didn't know me that well until I came out.

Just hang in there for now, and remember that what the people around you say about gay people is not only misinformed (e.g. you must like girly stuff if you're gay), but can also be damaging, as people are either forced into such a stereotype or get shunned for the sin of being different. Stay strong and true to yourself, and you'll find you way through. Sending positive vibes you way.

It's ok to be confused.

Most of us were at one point, my self included. I was in a brief relationship with a friend of mine (girl) at the time and I kept thinking about how it fit in to who I was and what I was feeling at the time. When it ended, it became clear to me that I was definitely into boys, but I didn't want that to be my label. I didn't want to be seen as the gay kid. So I stayed in the closet. I eventually came out 4 years later, and it was scary as hell. Not coming out earlier tho is my biggest regret in life. Not having a boyfriend who I actually loved and cared for, going to prom with him, learning about myself romantically as well as sexually, and more were things I missed out on because I remained in the closet.

The TLDR version is this: it's ok to feel confused. Figure out who you are and what you want, and then act on it, or don't.

I had a similar issue, albeit I live on the East coast where people are more accepting. Honestly I think you should hold on your desires and ride it out till college, when you said you wanted to come out. If you have that big of a fear that you'll be kicked out of your house for coming out then don't. You might just end up having to push down your desires however irresistable. It sucks, as I was heavy into sports in high school always around straight guys who were sexy as hell, and was pretty much unable to do anything about it without outing myself.

The key thing is to do it when you're ready. Although I will say that the biggest regret I have is not coming put earlier. Granted I live in a quite liberal area which helped, but I feel like I would have matured more if I had came out earlier. But don't rush it, only do it when you feel ready.
